subject: Regional data handover and retention SLA sync
messages:
From: Susan Mann <susan.mann@acmecloud.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acmecloud.com
Date: 2028-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft DPA - backlog questions on deletion windows

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for sending the DPA draft and Annex B. Legal ran a quick pass and we have a handful of open items specific to retention/deletion and geolocation handover. High level: Acme needs firm commitments on time-to-erasure for customer data and a clear playbook for certified deletion of backups.

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood confirm the maximum window between a customer deletion request and first-proof of erasure for primary data (we expect 30 days)?
- How are onshore/region copies handled (EU primary with US backups) — will backups be subject to the same SLA or a longer archival window?
- What evidence will Redwood provide when erasure is complete (signed manifest, hash list, or third-party attest)?

Attached is our markup of Annex B with Acme's preferred language (Acme_AnnexB_redline_20280510.docx).

We want to get alignment before we escalate to procurement. Can we schedule 30 minutes next week to walk the playbook?

Thanks,
Susan
Legal Ops
AcmeCloud

Attachments: Acme_AnnexB_redline_20280510.docx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Susan Mann <susan.mann@acmecloud.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA - backlog questions on deletion windows

Susan — thanks, and appreciate the clear list. Looping in Laura and Rishi for ops/legal detail.

Quick response / proposal from Redwood:
- Primary data: we can meet a 30-day certified erasure commitment for customer-owned primary datasets (30 calendar days from request). Certified erasure will include a deletion report and retention manifest.
- Backups: these are a tougher nut. Our suggested compromise: tombstone (logical delete) within 30 days, then physical deletion window of up to 180 days for archived replicas to allow for restore and disaster recovery. We will provide a certified deletion report once deletion completes.
- Onshore copies / geofallback: we propose that location-based replicas obey the same tombstone timing (30 days) but physical deletion timing can vary by region based on backup retention policies; we'll call this out in Annex B with a maximum physical destruction window.

Operational commitments we can include in Annex B:
- Erasure manifest delivered within 15 business days after deletion completes.
- Audit evidence: either internal deletion manifests or third-party attestation for periodic audits (annually).
- Legal hold carveouts: legal holds will pause the deletion workflow but we will provide visibility and evidence of the hold.

I've attached a suggested retention matrix that maps primary vs backup timelines and the manifest deliverable (redwood_proposed_retention_matrix.xlsx). Happy to walk through on a call.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_proposed_retention_matrix.xlsx

On Tue, May 12, 2028 at 11:03 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com> wrote:
> Susan — thanks, and appreciate the clear list. Looping in Laura and Rishi for ops/legal detail.
>
> Quick response / proposal from Redwood:
> - Primary data: we can meet a 30-day certified erasure commitment for customer-owned primary datasets (30 calendar days from request).

Hi all — adding a bit more ops-level color and an operational exception we need to call out.

Operational detail:
- Tombstone vs physical deletion: tombstone (logical remove from live indexes) occurs within 30 days for both primary and region-local replicas. Physical destruction for cold backups depends on how the snapshot/replication pipeline stores data — some snapshots are deduplicated and reside in cold storage where physical rewrite/overwrite occurs on a schedule.
- For EU-region customers where we maintain an EU primary and US cold copy as a DR fallback, our standard approach has been: tombstone within 30 days, then scheduled overwrite of cold copies during the next available maintenance window. In practice that can lead to a longer physical deletion wall-clock.

Proposed contract language to reduce ambiguity:
- Define two deadlines: "Proof of logical erasure" (within 30 days) and "Maximum physical destruction window" (we propose 180 days default, with an option for a shorter window by mutual agreement).
- For legal hold: deletion timelines will be paused and Redwood will provide a formal hold notice and status updates.

We should also document the forensic evidence we can produce (deletion manifests, snapshot IDs, storage job IDs) and commit to a playbook for handling evidence requests during audits. I've attached our erasure playbook (redwood_erasure_playbook_v1.pdf) for reference.

Happy to join a call to walk through the technical steps and the proposed phrasing.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Platform Operations
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Tom Perez <tom.perez@acmecloud.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Susan Mann <susan.mann@acmecloud.com>, legal@acmecloud.com
Date: 2028-05-17T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA - backlog questions on deletion windows

Vivek/Laura — thanks for the quick replies and the playbook. A few follow-ups from Acme's side after internal review:

- 180 days for physical deletion is longer than Acme is comfortable with for backups that contain EU customer data. We are willing to accept a short operational carveout for disaster recovery, but we need a hard cap of 90 days for physical destruction unless a formal legal hold applies.
- The manifest you propose is good, but we need the capability to request a certified erase report (signed PDF with job IDs + timestamps + hash where applicable) on demand; turnaround time expectation: 15 business days after request is reasonable — please confirm.
- For third-party assurance, Acme would prefer the option to require an independent deletion attestation (quarterly or on-demand for critical customers). Can Redwood include a process for engaging a third-party auditor?

I've summarized the Acme position in a short PDF (acme_feedback_summary.pdf). If you can accept the 90-day physical destruction cap and confirm the on-demand attestation flow, we can proceed to sign.

Thanks,
Tom Perez
Senior Counsel, AcmeCloud

Attachments: acme_feedback_summary.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Tom Perez <tom.perez@acmecloud.com>, Susan Mann <susan.mann@acmecloud.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-19T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA - backlog questions on deletion windows

Tom / Susan — appreciate the succinct feedback and the PDF. Quick summary of Redwood's counterproposal that I think lands between our asks:

1) Logical erasure (proof delivered): within 30 calendar days of request for primary and region-local replicas.
2) Tombstone confirmation for backups: tombstone (logical delete from catalogs/indexes) within 30 days.
3) Physical destruction: maximum of 90 days for cold backups containing EU customer data (reduced from our initial 180 days), unless a legal hold or regulatory requirement applies.
4) Evidence deliverables: certified erase report (signed PDF) delivered within 15 business days of Redwood completing the physical destruction. The report will include snapshot IDs, storage job IDs, deletion timestamps, and a manifest of affected objects.
5) Third-party attestation: Redwood will document a process to engage an independent retention/erasure attestation; on-demand attestations will be scoped and charged as professional services unless covered under an enterprise audit clause.

If that sounds acceptable, I'll circulate an updated Annex B with the 90-day max, legal-hold carveout language, and the evidence/playbook references. I'll also attach the DocuSign link for execution once we have a final Annex.

Next steps:
- I will draft the revised Annex B and retention matrix and circulate by EOD Monday.
- Proposed contract language will include the definitions: "logical erasure", "physical destruction", "legal hold", and "certified erase report" to avoid later ambiguity.

Thanks — let's aim to get this across the finish line this week.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com
